newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF says buys stake in Indonesian group.
newsitem.headline: SKF says buys stake in Indonesian group.

text.p: Swedish bearing maker SKF said on Tuesday it bought a 60 percent stake in Indonesia's leading bearing company PT Logan Sari Bearindo (LSB).

"For many years, SKF has been one of the foremost importers of rolling bearings to Indonesia," the company said in a statement. "The new Jakarta factory will enable SKF to also begin manufacturing in the country."
PT Federal Motor/PT Astra Dian Lestari, which belongs to Indonesian automotive group Astra, will keep 30 percent of shares, while the remainder is held by a few Indonesian shareholders, SKF said.
LSB's annual sales total $14.4 million and it has about 375 employees. Together with imports, SKF's total sales in Indonesia will exceed $35 million, the company said.

"We plan to coordinate the LSB factory's operation with our other operations in Asia," Gunnar Gremlin, president of SKF Asia Pacific Division, said. "These markets have top priority in the SKF group's strategy."
The Indonesian bearing market has recently experienced very strong development and currently has an annual growth rate of more than 10 percent, SKF said.
